newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL shares end near flat as GDP data discounted.
newsitem.headline: KL shares end near flat as GDP data discounted.

text.p: Malaysian shares closed almost unchanged as investors mostly discounted release of the country's gross domestic product growth of 8.2 percent for the first quarter of 1997, dealers and analysts said.
At the close the key Composite Index of 100 leading stocks dipped 0.79 of a point to 1,104.83, after having peaked at 1,111.77 earlier in the day.

"There has been profit taking today. The market has been fairly strong this week, so people are just locking in profits ahead of the weekend," said Victor Wan, senior analyst at South Johor Securities.
Malaysian central Bank Negara said on Friday the country's Gross Domestic Product for the first quarter in 1997 of 8.2 percent compared to 8.3 percent in the same period in 1996.
"The market was expecting 8.1, and it came out at 8.2, so there was not much concern. It shows the economy is still strong," said Wan.
Newly-listed packaging firm HPI Resources ended its first day of trading at 7.05 ringgit after debuting at 6.85 on an offer price of 3.10 ringgit.
Volume remained thin with 186 million shares traded, valued at 1,435 million ringgit. Losers outpaced gainers 323 to 224
Fund managers were closing their books for the month, inducing local funds to push up the market, said dealers.
"But someone came in in the afternoon and just started selling down blue chips including Telekom," said an institutional dealer at a local brokerage.
Telekom Malaysia closed down 20 cents at 18.60 ringgit.

National carrier Malaysian Airline closed five cents higher at 5.80. The company's net full year earnings released on Thursday beat market forecasts. But the inclusion of the proceeds of the sales of two aircraft dampened any euphoria on the stock, dealers said
"The release of some corporate results next week should inject some excitement into this market," said the dealer.

On the Kuala Lumpur Options and Financial Futures Exchange the spot May contract rose 6.2 points to 1,107.5 with 217 lots traded. The June futures contract ended 9.0 points higher at 1,107.0 with 828 lots changing hands.
